EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  JULY 22, 2019

A regular meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order by CHAIR HUFF at 7:00 p.m.

Committee Members Present:  Huff, Brtis, Ciarolla, Harik, Martin, Silvano, Shinn

Committee Members Absent:  Dean-Porter, Zigrang

City Staff Present: Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith

DRAFT MINUTES OF JUNE 24, 2019
MEMBER SILVANO moved, seconded by MEMBER SHINN

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE JUNE 24, 2019 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIR HUFF SO ORDERED.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
NONE

DISCUSSION ITEMS

A. CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE COMPANY WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT
MONTHLY UPDATE
ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER stated that the Trail Restoration Plan was included within
Agenda Materials and sent out to targeted group of people living along the trail as well as the
Equestrian Committee.

CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE COMPANY representative Angie Gilbride provided further
overview as follows:

  •  Remaining items for landscaping will be completed in the fall
  •  Paving of school parking lot, to be coordinate with school district and school, will be
  completed when all equipment is cleared
  •  Entrance of Palomino Trail by school – four sticks of pipe that need to be installed
  which will happen in the fall because of the testing still needed; the trail should be able
  to remain open during that time, however.
  1
 MEMBER BRTS expressed that the Restoration trail Plan does not provide detail as to why
some items are being done out of order, for instance tree stumps are still there.

CALWATER REPRESENTATIVE GILBRIDE will seek confirmation as to the process and
timeline to address tree stumps.

MEMBER BRTS explained that tree stumps across the trail are not down, but fence is being
installed. She further explained that she is concerned that the stumps are not going to be
grinded down by contractor. She asked if City staff uses asphalt for trails.

MAINTENANCE SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH explained that asphalt with clay is put on
trails over the dirt.

MEMBER BRTS recommended that City staff review what is happening in that area and
expressed concern with bringing horses home if some of these items are not fully complete.

CALWATER REPRESENTATIVE GILBRIDE explained that 20% is completed with shavings,
but expressed surprised that stumps are not cleared yet.

MEMBER SHINN requested something in writing that the stumps will be properly removed
with a timeline and what impacts that means to the community.

CALWATER REPRESENTATIVE GILBRIDE expressed that it is hard to put a concrete
timeline to it since construction can change daily. She further detailed that their project
superintendent was injured on the project site the week earlier and is out indefinitely but she
will work with the other staff on site to identify more information and provide further input to
the Committee.

ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER DAVIS stated that staff will work with CalWater on these items
as well. MAINTENANCE SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH added that he will go to the site
with CalWater staff to review the area and make recommendations as to the City’s process for
trail covering.

MEMBER SHINN asked when the landfill be reopened completely.

CALWATER REPRESENTATIVE GILBRIDE explained that the landfill is still used as a
staging site and likely won’t be completely cleared until next year.

AUDIENCE MEMBER BOB HUMPHREY expressed interest in Palomino trail from Rolling
Hills Road to the school to confirm this is accessible when horses return home. CALWATER
REPRESENTATIVE GILBRIDE confirmed it would be.

MEMBER BRTS asked if when people bring their horses home by the end of the month if it
was expected that they have to ride along the street; CALWATER REPRESENTATIVE
GILBRIDE responded that they have been told that the trail cover will be done by the end of

  2
 the month and that CalWater is pressing contractors and have emphasized this task as a high
priority.

AUDIENCE MEMBER Pam Schachter expressed that if crushed asphalt is used it needs to
be packed.

MAINTENANCE SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH explained that wood chips do not make
good cover but well- crushed asphalt is typical.

MEMBER BRTS requested that City staff review the area. MAINTENANCE
SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH affirmed.

MEMBER CIAROLLA asked that drainage and clay be considered so they horses do not sink.

B. CALIFORNIA DESPERADOS AND COWBOY MOUNTED SHOOTING ASSOCIATION -
MOUNTED SHOOTING COMPETITION AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK

COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO provided an overview per the
agenda material. Event organizer Brenda Caropino also provided an expanded overview of
her personal involvement in the community and the further explained the proposed event,
which she likened to a gymkhana event.

MS. CARAPINO explained that training with the Sheriff Posse had been done in the past at
Ernie Howlett park using a similar sounding soft air gun and riders in the area were
forewarned and no horses reacted to the sound. She further explained a study out of Moreno
Valley that expressed that the noise of this event is similar to a manual machine or vacuum
cleaner. She introduced Mark Caropino who is familiar with the event and helping to organize
the proposed event and Bill Hendrix who is an Assistant and also services on the Los Angeles
County Sheriff Posse.

MEMBER BRTS asked how dogs react to the sound. MS. CAROPINO explained that there
has not been a study on dogs’ reactions and that the focus has been on the horses. MR
CAROPINO explained that many people bring their dogs to the event and there have been no
adverse impacts. He further explained that the sound often cannot be heard within two
football fields away and it does not compare to a firework sound.

MEMBER SILVANO asked how often the shooting occurs throughout an event.

MS. CAROPINO explained that there is a staging area, participants are handed 10 cartridges,
guns stay in holsters during warm up and when the participant comes out shots are brief.
MEMBER MARTIN explained it takes about 30 seconds.

MEMBER SILVANO asked how long the event is expected to last. MS. CAROPINO
responded that the time of event would be from 9 or 10 am to 3:30 or 4 p.m. MR. HENDRIX
added that the event is no louder than a shooting range comparing the Redondo Beach Police
range, which is nearby a dog park.

AUDIENCE MEMBER SCHACHTER expressed that landfill noise can carry through the area.
  3
 MR. HENDRIX stated that based upon his experience, he does not believe the noise will
carry.

MEMBER CIAROLLA requested to see a demonstration, which was concurred by MEMBER
SHINN.

AUDIENCE MEMBER SCHACHTER asked what happens to the shells from the shooting.
MS. CAROPINO responded that there is no debris.

MEMBER HARIK stated that it does not seem like it would be louder than a baseball cage.
MR. HENDRIX affirmed and explained that a demonstration was done at a past City
Celebration.

MEMBER SHINN asked if the event tears up arena footing. MS. CAROPINO explained the
event only uses the sand area and the other arena is used for a slow-pace warm-up so there
is not an expected adverse impact to arena footing.

MEMBER SHINN requested a demonstration so the Committee could hear the gunfire sound
before making a decision.

The Committee discussed the option of holding a demonstration.

ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER recommended that the Committee hold a special meeting with
the Park and Activities Commission to view a demonstration and vote on the event.

MEMBER HARIK agreed that the City should consider this type of event and increase
involvement of the equestrian community.

AUDIENCE MEMBER SCHACHTER requested that if the event is approved by EC that the
following be considered:
  1- All equestrian area of the park be closed for a total cost of the event to be $1,000
  2- Stipulate posting of signs at least one week before and cover every entrance to
  park

MEMBER SHINN suggested that adjacent trails be closed; MEMBERS HARIK and MARTIN
disagreed.

MEMBER SILVANO moved, seconded by MEMBER SHINN

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE JUNE 24, 2019 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN HUFF SO ORDERED.

MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  THAT THE COMMITTEE HOLD A JOINT MEETING WITH THE PARK AND
  ACTIVITIES COMMISSION FOR THE PURPOSE OF A DEMONSTRATION AND A
  VOTE OF APPROVAL/DENIAL OF THE EVENT
  4
 THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIR HUFF SO ORDERED.

MEMBER MARTIN asked what day of the week the event was proposed. CHAIR HUFF
suggested the event be held on a Saturday. The Committee and event organizer concurred.

MEMBER SILVANO stated they want to support all forms of equestrian events.

STAFF ITEMS

A. EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER DAVIS explained the log consisted of concerns related to
manure rate increases and the City’s response as detailed in the log.

MEMBER BRTS expressed understanding of the concerns and explained her recognized
increases over the last year.

MEMBER SILVANO expressed that this was a topic of discussion a few years back and the
Committee was aware that prices were to be increased.

MEMBER CIAROLLA asked if the increase was related to a change in manure removal
business. ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER will confirm.

MEMBER SILVANO explained that at the time the information was presented, Waste
Management was losing money on the contract and the proposal was considering that all
trash rates would increase; she further detailed that the negotiation considered that manure
see an increase for cost recovery rather than spread the increase across all trash collection.

Committee members suggested that more information be available on the website, including
details about manure collection and rates.

AUDIENCE MEMBER SCHACHTER stated that a neighbor was informed by Waste
Management to mix manure with green waste. ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER responded that
this information does not seem to be correct but will confirm with Waste Management.

MEMBER SHINN stated that horses are expensive and manure is part of that cost.

MEMBER HARIK expressed that all residents should not have to pay for manure removal.

COMMITTEE REPORTS
A. CITY CELEBRATION SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING UPDATE

MEMBERS SHINN and CIAROLLA are helping with the trail course and getting organized.
MEMBER SILVANO indicated that the face painter and stick horses need to be confirmed and
that the City should assume those costs.

MEMBER SHINN stated that Channel 5 is likely to do a segment.

  5
 There was discussion of allowing the Queen Contest to be part of the event but it was the
consensus of the Committee that the Contest take place outside of the City Celebration. It
was suggested that if the Mounted Shooting event is approved, we request organizers to
provide a demonstration at the City Celebration.

B. ADOPT-A-TRAIL REPORT

MEMBER MARTIN stated that there is brush behind the Empty Saddle Club and there have
been concerns raised by the Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy. ASSISTANT CITY
MANAGER DAVIS will follow-up.

MEMBER BRTIS explained that the trail behind the little league field is overgrown.
MAINTENACE SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH explained that the area is on the list for
maintenance.

MEMBER SILVANO stated that the new footing in the dressage arena is good. She also
indicated that the judge’s booth gets very hot.

MEMBER OF THE AUDIENCE added that the steps of the judge’s booth are hard to see.

MAINTENACE SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH stated that we can add a ceiling fan and
that grip tape will be placed on steps.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
  A. PV PENINSULA WATER RELIABILTY PROJECT UPDATE – monthly

  B. CITY CELEBRATION UPDATE

ADJOURNMENT
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO ADJOURN TO A SPECIAL JOINT MEETING OF THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITEE
  AND PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIR HUFF ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 8:11PM

Respectfully submitted,

Alexa Davis
Assistant City Manager

  6
